title: Can the dividing CIPS condensates' self-made amphiphile layer do work (gate the fuel), and can the population keep dividing once the box is full (deaths)?
summary: c40's dividing CIPS world (20261026T1100-c40-cips-layered-divide-claim) gives layered bodies that divide on a consumed fuel and die without it, but the s layer is passive (one-way coupled) and division stops once the bodies fill the box at the lever-rule area fraction, with no deaths. Two one-loop experiments: (1) let s gate fuel transport, DF_face = DF exp(-beta s) with a harmonic face mean (TOOLBOX exponential gate), beta in {0.05, 0.2} at the world's defaults, seed 0, t=12000; measure fuel inside vs outside bodies, body size and division rate against beta=0, and whether the gate changes the division size (the layer would then do work, scored under mechanism). (2) Make the box non-stationary so that births keep balancing deaths: slow periodic fuel supply kF(t) = 0.2 (1 + 0.5 sin(2 pi t / 4000)), or a 2x larger box with a lower e0 so territory stays free longer; count births and deaths per 2000 t over t=10000-30000 on 2 seeds.
experiment: Fuel gate: add DF exp(-beta s) (harmonic face mean) to world.py's fuel step (explicit correction on top of the spectral step, as in xgenome perm), run beta in {0, 0.05, 0.2}, seed 0, 192^2, t=12000; report fuel in/out of bodies, mean body area, persistent splits. Turnover: periodic kF with period 4000 at the defaults, seeds 0-1, t=30000; report births and deaths (labkit lineage) per 2000 t.
